title: Deduction for Protection Cover That Cannot Travel With a Northbeam Renew Trade-In Batch
content:
The cover deduction follows the protection cover the profile holds on the batch, because a batch whose cover cannot travel with the machines is worth less on resale than one whose cover can, and a plan whose own claim is still under review may yet pay out on those machines, which leaves less of the cover to lose. The cover in question is a plan held under Northbeam ShieldCare Protection Plans on the serial standing on the Renew trade-in agreement, and whether that cover may be transferred with the machines is read from the plan's own record.

| The protection cover held on the batch | The cover deduction |
| --- | --- |
| a protection plan standing active on the batch whose cover may not be transferred | the untransferable cover deduction, 220.00 USD |
| a protection plan standing in claim hold on the batch whose cover may not be transferred | the held cover deduction, 90.00 USD |
| no protection plan on the batch standing active or in claim hold, or cover on it that may be transferred with the machines | nothing |

**Reading the two conditions.** Each of the first two branches is a pair: the state the plan stands in, and that the cover on it may not be transferred. A plan standing active whose cover may be transferred falls into the third row, and so does a plan standing in any state other than active or claim hold, whatever its transfer terms.

**Basis questions.**

*Why is the deduction smaller where the plan stands in claim hold?* Because a plan whose own claim is still under review may yet pay out on those machines, which leaves less of the cover to lose.

*Is the deduction taken per machine?* No. It is one amount against the batch: 220.00 USD or 90.00 USD, or nothing.

*What settles whether the cover may travel?* The plan's own record under Northbeam ShieldCare Protection Plans, matched to the serial standing on the trade-in agreement, and not the customer's account of what the plan allows.
